questions.title: Singleton Pattern Intent
questions.question: What is the Singleton design pattern and when would you use it?
questions.realWorldScenario: A configuration manager, database connection pool, or logger — one instance shared across the application.

questions.title: Eager vs Lazy Singleton
questions.question: What is the difference between eager and lazy singleton initialization in Java?
searchIntent: eager vs lazy singleton initialization Java
questions.realWorldScenario: Choosing when to create an expensive object — at startup (eager) or on first use (lazy).

questions.title: Thread-Safe Singleton
questions.question: How do you make a Singleton thread-safe in Java? What is double-checked locking?
questions.realWorldScenario: Multiple threads trying to create the first instance simultaneously — race condition.

questions.title: Enum as Singleton
questions.question: Why is using an enum the recommended way to implement Singleton in Java?
searchIntent: how to use enum for singleton Java
questions.realWorldScenario: Effective Java Item 3 — the enum approach is serialisation-safe and prevents reflection attacks.

questions.title: Spring Beans Are Singletons
questions.question: How does Spring's default bean scope relate to the Singleton pattern?
questions.realWorldScenario: Understanding that @Service and @Repository annotated classes are singletons by default in Spring.

questions.title: Singleton Anti-Patterns
questions.question: What are the drawbacks of the Singleton pattern and why is it sometimes called an anti-pattern?
questions.realWorldScenario: Global state in Singletons makes unit testing hard — you cannot easily mock a true Singleton.
